verdict.reasoning: Patient reports sudden inability to move the left arm: "I woke up this morning about an hour ago and I couldn't move my left arm anymore." and later confirms "The arm still can't move."
Onset one hour prior and non-painful: "I woke up this morning about an hour ago and I couldn't move my left arm anymore" and "I feel no pain, but just can't move it."
Patient states: "I feel a bit of tingling on the left side of my face."

Difficulty swallowing inferred from drinking problems: Patient says, "I was trying to drink earlier and I dribbled a bit" and doctor says, "so you had some difficulty swallowing, is that right?" Patient responds, "Yeah."
Patient reports slowed speech: "Any problems with your speech?..." Patient: "Yeah, it feels a bit harder. It's more complicated. Maybe be more slow. I need to think more about it."
No prior episodes: Doctor asks, "Has this ever happened before?" Patient replies, "No, no, it's really the first time."
Patient states: "I have type 2 diabetes".
Patient adds: "and high blood pressure." which corresponds to hypertension.
On medications: Patient says, "I'm taking metformin, losartan, and amlodipine."
Same quote: "I'm taking metformin, losartan, and amlodipine."
Same quote: "I'm taking metformin, losartan, and amlodipine."
On allergies: Doctor asks, "Do you have any allergies to any medication?" Patient: "Only penicillin, I believe."
Family history: Patient says, "My dad has got heart disease, but I don't know more detail."
Smoking: Doctor asks, "Do you smoke at all?" Patient replies, "I used to." indicating former smoker.
Alcohol: Patient says, "I will have a few drinks over the weekend, maybe a couple more during the week." and specifies "Beers. Like pints." which matches moderate beer consumption mainly on weekends.
Living situation: Doctor asks, "And are you normally living alone?" Patient: "Yes."
Persistent left arm deficit: initial "I couldn't move my left arm anymore" and later, "How are you feeling now?..." Patient: "The arm still can't move."
No facial asymmetry or discoloration: Doctor asks about facial asymmetry; patient replies, "No, not really." Doctor also asks, "Is there any discoloration in your hand?" Patient: "No."
No leg symptoms: Doctor asks, "Have you had any symptoms in your left leg at all?" Patient: "No."
Speech abnormality: Patient says, "Yeah, it feels a bit harder. It's more complicated. Maybe be more slow." This supports slurred or slowed speech as a clinical summary.
Difficulty swallowing: Doctor confirms, "so you had some difficulty swallowing, is that right?" and patient answers, "Yeah."

Doctor states concern for stroke: "I'm concerned that some of the symptoms you've got may be some symptoms of a stroke." Symptoms described include acute left arm non-movement (hemiparesis), left facial tingling (sensory), and speech difficulty (dysphasia), supporting the summarized assessment.

Emergency ambulance: Patient asks, "Would you be able to call the ambulance for me?" Doctor: "I'm happy to do that… I'm going to arrange one of my colleagues next to me to call an ambulance to your home address now."

Access advice: Doctor says, "maybe you could leave the front door unlocked to sit in the hallway" and later, "Just make sure that the front door is open. Sit in the hallway by the front door so that they've got access."
The doctor says the ambulance will "probably take you down to the local hospital, a e," but the transcript does not confirm that the patient was actually transported.

The transcript mentions that the ambulance will call the stroke doctor "to assess you, to see whether they can give you any kind of treatment," but does not state that symptoms were to be monitored en route or specifically that preparations were made for thrombolysis or stroke team intervention.
